facts.label: legend
facts.quote: The Kurukshetra in Haryana is the battlefield of Mahabharata and all the soil there is still red because of the blood of the people who died in the War.
facts.text: Popular regional legend asserts that the reddish hue observed in patches of Kurukshetra's soil was caused by the blood of millions of warriors killed in the epic battle.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: cakravyūho mahārāja ācāryeṇābhikalpitaḥ tatra śakropamāḥ sarve rājāno viniveśitāḥ.
facts.text: According to the Drona Parva of the Mahabharata, Acharya Drona arrayed the Kaurava army into the circular Cakravyuha on the thirteenth day of the Kurukshetra war.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: While still in his mother's womb, Abhimanyu overheard Arjuna discussing the method to penetrate the formation but did not learn the means to exit it.
facts.text: The Drona Parva states that Abhimanyu possessed the knowledge to pierce and enter the Chakravyuh because he had overheard Arjuna explaining the technique while still in his mother's womb, but lacked the knowledge of how to escape it.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Half of this will be in the form of a cart and half in the form of a lotus. There will be an array in the form of a needle in the midst of the pericarp of the lotus.
facts.text: On the fourteenth day of the war, Drona arranged a hybrid tactical array consisting of half a cart and half a lotus with an inner needle-shaped formation to safeguard Jayadratha, describing dynamic troop maneuvers rather than a rigid stone maze.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: It bears a legend written in Sanskrit language and Brahmi script of about 1st century CE.
facts.text: An inscribed terracotta seal written in Sanskrit using 1st-century CE Brahmi script was recovered from the archaeological mound at Amin.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Sub-period IB: overlap between late Harappan and Painted Grey Ware (PGW) culture (c. 1400–1000 BCE).
facts.text: Excavations conducted by J. P. Joshi of the Archaeological Survey of India at Bhagwanpura in Kurukshetra revealed an overlapping occupational sequence between Late Harappan and Painted Grey Ware cultures dated to between 1400 BCE and 1000 BCE.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The excavation revealed a single phase culture of PG Ware alongwith its associated materials.
facts.text: Excavations at Harsh-ka-Tila in Thanesar, Kurukshetra, led by B. M. Pande of the Archaeological Survey of India, established continuous habitation layers spanning from the Painted Grey Ware period up through the late medieval period.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The carvings on the Halebidu temple of Mysore that was supposed to have constructed during the 12th and 13th centuries A.D. contain a structure of Chakravyuh.
facts.text: The earliest well-documented Indian stone relief depicting the classical seven-tier labyrinth pattern associated with the Chakravyuh dates to the 12th or 13th century CE on the outer wall of the Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Indian archaeologist BB Lal, who carried out extensive excavations in the 1950s at places such as Indraprastha and Hastinapur, has estimated that the epic battle in Kurukshetra could have taken place around 800 BC.
facts.text: Scholars disagree over the historical timeframe of the Kurukshetra conflict, with archaeologists like B. B. Lal proposing a date around 800 BCE based on Painted Grey Ware excavations, while traditional astronomers argue for a date around 3102 BCE.
